evidence: Frozen task/environment/instructions/integration.md:3 states node /app/server.js, arbitrary launch CWD, 0.0.0.0:3000, / and GET /api/health; these match tests/test.sh:47-55,97-111 and the restart launch. integration.md:5 supplies Node 22, Express, better-sqlite3 through NODE_PATH and requires runtime-complete output; both Dockerfiles install matching Express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1. integration.md:7,9 disclose /assets/seed_data.json, /app/app.db, DB_PATH override and writable-copy execution; test.sh:90-111 implements the copy and override. integration.md:11 explicitly states exactly the symlink restriction enforced at test.sh:72-83. instruction.md:3 incorporates all six notes. PORT=3000 supplies the stated fixed port; PATH/HOME and unprivileged ownership are shared launch housekeeping rather than an additional product obligation. test.sh is byte-identical to frozen template. Checked all eight current index artifact hashes and all 16 source hashes quoted in row19-runtime-probe.log: all match current bytes. That log (SHA256 f20452fe5b990c4687c760c89bbb3c5a61a946a1f92b2173d46eb99ff17ea2d8), whose probe code was inspected, observes unprivileged env-i startup from /tmp, root/assets/health, default DB, custom DB_PATH, relocated app and restart persistence; RESULT reports all true, EXIT 0. It uses the agent image and a slightly different PATH/HOME, so it is partial corroboration, not exact test.sh/full configured grading. Alternative considered: hardcoded disclosed port with custom API routes/local bundled dependencies remains launch-compatible; no hidden route or dependency demand was found. Broken health-only/static app can satisfy permissive readiness (even HTTP error), but readiness is merely a transport precheck before the gates, not a row-23 runtime-contract mismatch. No full judge, portal or score claim is made.
